scope: audit-only; does not authorize object identity, attributes, delivery edges, or Unit uses

reviews.summaryEvidence: A Deployment Skill that lets the user place carried Weapons or Equipment
factsEvidence: When the user deploys, they may place the allowed number of carried Weapons or Equipment
reviews.caveat: Minelayer is a deployment method for the user's source-listed items, not a separate deployed-object identity. It cannot authorize a generic Mine variant or reverse Unit ownership.

reviews.summaryEvidence: A Common Skill used to place eligible
factsEvidence: The user places one eligible Token or Model without a Roll
reviews.caveat: Place Deployable defines a placement method for eligible source-listed items; its generic Token/Model wording is not a new object identity or a blanket delivery edge.

factsEvidence: During the Active Turn, place two 55 mm Speedball Tokens
Request Speedball cannot be performed partway through the Order Expenditure Sequence.
reviews.caveat: N5.3 p. 84 explicitly defines Speedball Tokens as State Tokens for support drops, not as standard targetable Deployable Weapon/Equipment profiles. The Tokens and their single-use contents have no reviewed ARM/BTS/STR/S source profile here and must not receive inferred reverse uses.

reviews.summaryEvidence: A Token represents a [[trait:deployable|Deployable]] Weapon or piece of Equipment on the battlefield.
reviews.caveat: Glossary term for an on-table representation, not a separate object profile. Resolve any particular Token to its actual source Weapon or Equipment and reviewed delivery before publishing uses.

reviews.summaryEvidence: This token is a reminder placed to indicate the effect of a rule, Skill, or game state
reviews.caveat: A State Token indicates an effect and is not automatically a targetable Deployable. Specific Speedball and SpecBall tokens are classified by their own source clauses.

reviews.summaryEvidence: Equipment with the [[trait:deployable|Deployable]] Trait can be placed as an independent battlefield game element
reviews.caveat: Generic Deployable Equipment terminology provides neither a concrete Equipment identity nor four-attribute values; review each source item separately.

reviews.summaryEvidence: A Weapon with the [[trait:deployable|Deployable]] Trait can be placed as an independent battlefield game element
reviews.caveat: Generic Deployable Weapon terminology is not an object instance or source-specific delivery edge; source Weapon and mode must be verified separately.

reviews.summaryEvidence: A Scenery Element is a battlefield game element representing scenery or terrain
reviews.caveat: Scenery Element is a class of battlefield game elements, not one universal scenery profile. Deployable Cover remains a separately reviewed S3 example; other scenery requires its own source evidence.

reviews.summaryEvidence: Place the 55 mm Token via [[skill:combat-jump|Combat Jump]] with PH 15
factsEvidence: Outside the [[rule:order-expenditure-sequence|Order Expenditure Sequence]], place one 55 mm SpecBall Token
SpecBall Tokens are [[term:state-token|State Tokens]]: they do not block enemy Movement and cannot be selected as targets for [[equipment:deactivator|Deactivators]].
reviews.caveat: N5.3 p. 98 describes one SpecBall State Token collected by an eligible Spec-Ops Trooper; it is distinct from the two Speedballs in Request Speedball (p. 84). Neither drop Token is a standard targetable four-attribute Deployable. A SpecBot selected as a SpecBall item requires separate evidence and is not classified here.

reviews.summaryEvidence: assigns the user's profile-listed MODs to one deployed Remote
factsEvidence: When the user is deployed, the player places a RemDriver Token beside one Remote already deployed on the game table.
The RemDriver Token is removed at the end of the Order in which the user enters any Null State.
reviews.caveat: RemDriver Token marks a Remote receiving MODs from a separate Trooper. It is not an independently deployed Weapon/Equipment profile, delivery edge or additional Remote carrier.

reviews.summaryEvidence: A Peripheral type with unlimited operating distance that starts undeployed
factsEvidence: An Ancillary [[skill:peripheral|Peripheral]] does not deploy with its Controller. The Controller may place it later using [[skill:place-deployable|Place Deployable]]
reviews.caveat: N5.3 pp. 107-108 explicitly allow a Controller to place its Ancillary Peripheral, which then uses Peripheral activation rules. This is a Peripheral Trooper with its own source Unit/Profile relationships, not a Weapon/Equipment four-stat object or generic source-weapon reverse use. Whether a dedicated peripheral-object reference is needed remains open.

factsEvidence: Keep the Supply Box Token on the table even if its carrier becomes classified as Null.
reviews.caveat: Supply Box Tokens belong to the core Supplies scenario, with scenario-specific representation, carrying and control rules. They are concrete objective elements, not source Weapon/Equipment Deployables or Army roster items; an objective catalog would need separate provenance and presentation.

reviews.summaryEvidence: A Short Skill used by Specialist Troops to collect a Supply Box.
factsEvidence: The Specialist must be in Silhouette contact with a Supply Box Token not being carried by a Model
reviews.caveat: Pick Up Supply Boxes is a scenario Skill acting on a Supplies objective. It creates no additional Supply Box identity, general Deployable placement edge, or Weapon/Equipment Unit use.
